problem: Prior audio-visual navigation (AV-Nav, AV-WaN, SAVi) assumes a clean, static, single sound source, fuses audio and vision only by feature concatenation into a GRU, and generalizes poorly to unheard sounds.
motivation: Real scenarios involve moving targets (people, pets), noisy audio and distractor sounds, which make earlier observations stale and require proactive interception. Spectrograms also carry geometric information (room layout) that could be fused spatially with an occupancy map to generalize better.
key_idea: Fuse binaural audio and the egocentric-built allocentric geometric map in a shared spatial feature space (Spatial Audio Encoder + Audio-Visual Encoder), and train with randomized complex audio scenarios on a new dynamic moving-sound benchmark.
insight: Training with complex audio scenarios (second sound, distractors, SpecAugment) gives large gains on unheard sounds across all models (e.g. Replica static unheard SR 58.5 to 77.8 for the proposed model), and the components are complementary across datasets (Tab. S.1/S.2). Removing the audio-spatial encoder drops performance (Tab. S.5), and the plain distance reward works better than the oracle-intersection reward for dynamic sounds (Tab. S.6/S.7).
method: Dynamic AudioGoal task: the sound source follows the shortest path to random goals, moving to the next node with 30% probability per step; the agent must call Stop at the source's position.
DSPL/DSNA metrics: SPL/SNA computed against the earliest reachable intersection with the target trajectory (oracle upper bound).
Reward: +10 on success, ±0.25 dense reward for change in geodesic distance to the current source position, -0.01 per step.
Complex audio scenarios: per-episode second sound at the goal, per-step random distractor sound at random locations, and random SpecAugment time/frequency masking, using only training sounds.

Spatial audio-visual fusion: a transposed-conv Spatial Audio Encoder maps the binaural spectrogram to spatial features that are concatenated with the allocentric geometric map (explored/occupied channels built from depth) and convolved by an Audio-Visual Encoder; a GRU also takes depth and audio encodings.
Policy: PPO chooses waypoints from a 3x3 action map (reduced from AV-WaN's 9x9) executed by a Dijkstra planner, so at most four observations go unprocessed.

setting.backbone: CNN encoders + GRU with PPO (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: RL in SoundSpaces on Replica (9 train scenes) and Matterport3D (59 train scenes) with 73 training sounds (102 sounds split 73/11/18); dynamic training uses half static and half moving episodes; complex-audio randomization for '+comp' variants
setting.observation: egocentric depth (RGB also given) + binaural spectrogram; allocentric geometric map built from depth
setting.action_space: predicted local waypoints (3x3 action map) executed by a Dijkstra planner over Move Forward / Rotate Left / Rotate Right / Stop
setting.privileged: none (map built online from depth; pose assumed available for mapping)

numbers_note: The split names 'heard'/'unheard' refer to sounds in unseen scenes; mapped to test-unseen as an approximation since the paper does not label the split as val or test. Only the main rows are listed; static complex-scenario test results are in Tab. III.
results: On the static AudioGoal benchmark with unheard sounds, the method plus complex-scenario training improves SR from the best baseline's 57.1 (AV-Nav) to 77.8 on Replica and from 54.6 (AV-WaN) to 70.6 on MP3D. On dynamic unheard sounds SR rises from 38.2 to 67.3 on Replica and from 47.2 to 74.0 on MP3D over the best clean-trained baseline (AV-WaN). It is consistently best on unheard sounds, though not always on heard sounds.
limitations: Simulation only, with a simple goal-directed motion model for the source, which is unaffected by the agent and has no embodiment or orientation.
Complex-audio training lowers performance on heard sounds in Replica, and the benefit varies across datasets and components.
DSPL is an oracle upper bound that may be unattainable without knowing the target trajectory.
